distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：It can turn something boring into something interesting. 称涂画能化无聊为有趣，但 doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention 只说在乏味讲座中涂画能助你专注，并未说讲座因此变有趣——是"帮你听下去"，不是"让它变好玩"。

records.stem: What is characteristic of people with drawing talent?
records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 What is characteristic of people with drawing talent? 问的是有绘画天赋的人具有什么特征，原文必有明示。
【拆句】 What is characteristic of people with drawing talent? 主干 what is characteristic of X，characteristic 在此为形容词，介词 of 引出 X，句式简洁无陷阱。
【定位】 P7 There's also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists. 也有证据表明，绘画才能取决于一个人感知世界的准确程度。人类视觉系统常误判大小、形状、颜色和角度，但艺术家能比非艺术家更准确地感知这些特性。
【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Sensitivity to cognitive stimulation. 称对认知刺激敏感，但 P7 谈的是视觉感知（visual perception）的准确度，并未涉及对认知刺激（cognitive stimulation）的敏感度——cognitive stimulation 是来自第 6 段涂画/默认回路话题的措辞。 B) 与原文相反 Subtlety of representation. 称表现手法精巧，但 We mistakenly think of "good" drawings as those which work as recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions 明确表示"把绘画当作现实再现"是错误归类；且本题问的是绘画者的特征而非作品的特征。 C) 偷换概念 Accuracy in categorization. 称分类的准确性，但 P7 说的是感知（perception）的准确性，并非分类（categorization）能力；文章中 categorization 一词只出现在第 4 段讨论绘画的"归类"问题，与艺术家的视觉能力无关。 D) ✓ 正确 artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists ↔ Precision in visual perception. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles ↔ Precision in visual perception. 选项 D 把原文"perceive more accurately"整体名词化为"precision in visual perception"，是定位句的最简同义替换。
records.keyword_relation: artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists ↔ Precision in visual perception.；The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles ↔ Precision in visual perception.

evidence.text: There's also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists

distractor_explanations.A: 张冠李戴：Sensitivity to cognitive stimulation. 称对认知刺激敏感，但 P7 谈的是视觉感知（visual perception）的准确度，并未涉及对认知刺激（cognitive stimulation）的敏感度——cognitive stimulation 是来自第 6 段涂画/默认回路话题的措辞。
distractor_explanations.B: 与原文相反：Subtlety of representation. 称表现手法精巧，但 We mistakenly think of "good" drawings as those which work as recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions 明确表示"把绘画当作现实再现"是错误归类；且本题问的是绘画者的特征而非作品的特征。
distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：Accuracy in categorization. 称分类的准确性，但 P7 说的是感知（perception）的准确性，并非分类（categorization）能力；文章中 categorization 一词只出现在第 4 段讨论绘画的"归类"问题，与艺术家的视觉能力无关。

records.stem: What does the author say about car advertisements?

options.text: They portray drivers who enjoy speed on the road.
They present a false picture of the autonomy cars provide.
They pursue individuality and originality in design concept.
They overestimate the potential market of autonomous cars.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What does the author say about car advertisements 直接问作者对广告的具体表述，无 infer/imply 等推断信号，属对原文某句的客观转述。
【拆句】 标准 What does the author say about X 句式，宾语从句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】 P1 There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads. 广告中那种"脱离现实"的味道几乎让人觉得有趣——量产车被包装成个性与自由的象征，可它们这辈子大多数时间都堵在短途的拥挤路上。
【选项】 A) 无中生有 原文谈的是个性 / 自由的形象与拥堵现实的反差，没有任何句子说广告里的司机享受速度。 B) ✓ 正确 detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom ↔ They present a false picture of the autonomy cars provide 预判要的"广告呈现的自由是失真的"，B 恰好以 false picture + autonomy 两词整齐对应原文，是定位句的同义压缩。 C) 偷换概念 原文说广告把车包装为"个性的象征"（marketed as symbols of individuality），不是说广告在"设计理念上追求个性与原创"。 D) 张冠李戴 原文谈的是普通量产车广告，autonomous cars（自动驾驶车）要到 P5 才出现，且与广告无关。
records.keyword_relation: detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom ↔ They present a false picture of the autonomy cars provide

evidence.text: There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads

distractor_explanations.A: 无中生有：原文谈的是个性 / 自由的形象与拥堵现实的反差，没有任何句子说广告里的司机享受速度。
distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：原文说广告把车包装为"个性的象征"（marketed as symbols of individuality），不是说广告在"设计理念上追求个性与原创"。
distractor_explanations.D: 张冠李戴：原文谈的是普通量产车广告，autonomous cars（自动驾驶车）要到 P5 才出现，且与广告无关。

records.stem: What does the author imply about the various gadgets on cars?

options.text: They can help to alleviate traffic jams.
Most of them are as effective as advertised.
Only some can be put to use under current traffic conditions.
They are constantly upgraded to make driving easier and safer.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （推断题）
【判型】 What does the author imply about the various gadgets on cars 中 imply 是典型推断信号，要求在原文未明说的方向上做一步延伸。
【拆句】 What does the author imply about X 标准句式，结构无难度，关键是认出 imply 的题型信号。
【定位】 P2 For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams. 尽管人们对极速、过弯和加速大谈特谈，但现代车上真正有用的小装置，反而都是在你开得很慢时才派上用场的那些——停车感应、音响、导航。
【选项】 A) 过度推断 原文说导航 apps 能 spot 拥堵并 suggest ways round，但下一段立刻指出这只是把堵车"转移"到 side roads，并未真正缓解（alleviate）。 B) 无中生有 原文只罗列 gadgets 哪些有用，并没有把它们与广告所宣传的效果做比较，无从得出"多数与广告一样有效"。 C) ✓ 正确 the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly ↔ Only some can be put to use under current traffic conditions 预判要的"只有一部分装置真正派用"，C 用 only some 精准对上原文 those which... 的子集限定，是唯一吻合预判的选项。 D) 无中生有 原文没有讨论 gadgets "不断升级"，更未涉及"让驾驶更轻松/安全"的整体趋势。
records.keyword_relation: the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly ↔ Only some can be put to use under current traffic conditions

evidence.text: For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams

distractor_explanations.A: 过度推断：原文说导航 apps 能 spot 拥堵并 suggest ways round，但下一段立刻指出这只是把堵车"转移"到 side roads，并未真正缓解（alleviate）。
distractor_explanations.B: 无中生有：原文只罗列 gadgets 哪些有用，并没有把它们与广告所宣传的效果做比较，无从得出"多数与广告一样有效"。
distractor_explanations.D: 无中生有：原文没有讨论 gadgets "不断升级"，更未涉及"让驾驶更轻松/安全"的整体趋势。

records.stem: What does the author say about the use of navigation apps?

options.text: It is likely to create traffic jams in other places.
It helps a great deal in easing traffic congestion.
It sharply reduces the incidence of traffic accidents.
It benefits those who are learning to drive.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 What does the author say about the use of navigation apps 用 say 而非 imply，属客观转述类细节题。
【拆句】 What does the author say about the use of X 标准句式，宾语是动名词短语 the use of navigation apps，平铺无陷阱。
【定位】 P3 But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them. 但当所有人都掌握完美信息时，堵车只会蔓延到那些看起来能绕开拥堵的次要道路上去。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them ↔ It is likely to create traffic jams in other places 预判要的"导航把堵车推到别处"，A 用 create traffic jams + in other places 精准对应 spread onto + the side roads，是定位句的同义改写。 B) 与原文相反 原文核心是导航 apps 只能把堵车搬走、不能从总量上 ease it；选项却说"对缓解拥堵帮助巨大"，与作者立场相反。 C) 无中生有 原文全段讨论的是"避堵"，从未涉及"交通事故发生率"，更没说能 sharply reduce。 D) 偷换概念 原文未提"学车人"这一群体，只笼统说 everyone / a lucky few；选项偷换为"对学车者有益"。
records.keyword_relation: traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them ↔ It is likely to create traffic jams in other places

evidence.text: But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them

distractor_explanations.B: 与原文相反：原文核心是导航 apps 只能把堵车搬走、不能从总量上 ease it；选项却说"对缓解拥堵帮助巨大"，与作者立场相反。
distractor_explanations.C: 无中生有：原文全段讨论的是"避堵"，从未涉及"交通事故发生率"，更没说能 sharply reduce。
distractor_explanations.D: 偷换概念：原文未提"学车人"这一群体，只笼统说 everyone / a lucky few；选项偷换为"对学车者有益"。

records.stem: What does the author say about technology?

options.text: Its consequences are usually difficult to assess.
It seldom delivers all the benefits as promised.
It depends on the required knowledge for application.
Its benefits are guaranteed by collective wisdom.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What does the author say about technology 仍是 say 句式，要求转述作者对 technology 的明确表述。

records.stem: What is the conclusion of a recently-published report?

options.text: Natural sciences should be learned the way humanities courses are.
Cultivation of creativity should permeate the entire school curriculum.
Art courses should be made compulsory for all students.
Students should learn more obviously creative subjects.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What is the conclusion of a recently-published report? 指向报告里一句明确的判断，是定点细节题。
【拆句】 Q47 主干 What is the conclusion，of a recently-published report 是后置定语；结构平铺，无陷阱。
【定位】 P2 The report concludes that creativity should not inhabit the school curriculum only as it relates to drama, music, art and other obviously creative subjects, but that creative thinking ought to run through all of school life, infusing(充满) the way humanities and natural sciences are learned. 该报告得出结论：创造力不应只在戏剧、音乐、美术等明显属于创意类科目中出现于学校课程，相反，创造性思维应贯穿整个校园生活，渗透到人文学科和自然科学的学习方式中。
【选项】 A) 无中生有 Natural sciences should be learned the way humanities courses are. 凭空规定自然科学要按人文学科的方式学习——原文只说创造性思维渗透两者的学习方式，并未让一者照搬另一者。 B) ✓ 正确 creative thinking ought to run through all of school life ↔ Cultivation of creativity should permeate the entire school curriculum. infusing(充满) the way humanities and natural sciences are learned ↔ permeate the entire school curriculum B 项把 run through all of school life 改写为 permeate the entire school curriculum，是 but 后内容的精准同义复述。 C) 偷换概念 Art courses should be made compulsory for all students. 把原文“创造性思维渗透全部课程”偷换为“艺术课必须成为必修”，原文从未提到 compulsory。 D) 与原文相反 Students should learn more obviously creative subjects. 恰好是结论 not A but B 中被否定的 A——原文反对“只把创造力限制在明显的创意学科里”，选项却让学生多学这些学科。

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 What does the report say is detrimental to the fostering of creativity? 问的是报告里点名的具体不利因素，是定点细节。
【拆句】 Q48 主干 What does the report say is detrimental to ...；嵌套了 say 引导的宾语从句，从句主语正是答案所指。理解时把 say 看作透明引述即可。
【定位】 P3 When children are regarded as vessels to be filled with facts, creativity does not prosper; nor does it when teachers' sole objective is coaching children towards exams. 当孩子被看作待填装事实的容器时，创造力无法繁荣；当教师的唯一目标是辅导孩子应对考试时，创造力同样无法繁荣。
【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Alleviation of pressure. 借用了段中的 alleviate 一词，但原文是说要“缓解”应试取向带来的问题——alleviation 本身是正面行为，不可能是 detrimental。 B) 与原文相反 Teacher-led school activities. 取自原文里报告的正面建议 a network of teacher-led “creativity collaboratives”，却被当作有害因素，与原文极性相反。 C) ✓ 正确 teachers' sole objective is coaching children towards exams ↔ Test-oriented teaching. the uninspiring and fact-based approach to education ↔ Test-oriented teaching. C 项把段中两处对应内容压缩为 Test-oriented teaching，是报告明确点名的负面教学方式。 D) 无中生有 Independent learning. 完全没有原文依据——第三段根本未讨论 independent learning 是否有害。

records.stem: What should be done to meet the future challenges?

options.text: Increasing government investment in school education.

【判型】 What should be done to meet the future challenges? 表面像主旨，但实质问的是末段给出的对策，是定点细节。
【拆句】 Q50 主干 What should be done，to meet the future challenges 是不定式状语，表目的；句子无陷阱。
【定位】 P5 As lives are affected by any number of looming challenges—climate crisis, automation in the workplace—humans are going to need creative thinking more than ever. For all of our sakes, creativity in education, and for all, must become a priority. 由于人类生活正受各种正在逼近的挑战——气候危机、工作场所自动化——所影响，我们将比以往任何时候都更需要创造性思维。为了我们所有人，教育中的创造力，并惠及所有人，必须成为重中之重。

records.stem: What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation?

options.text: Repeat what their partners say one way or another.
Focus as much as possible on topics of mutual interest.
Imitate their partners' gestures without their knowing it.
Observe carefully how their partners make use of gestures.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation? 是 What...do 句式，问的是客观行为，无 infer/imply/mainly 等推断或主旨信号词。
【拆句】 What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation? 主干是 What do people tend to do，宾语从句式 What 提问；while engaging in a conversation 是分词短语作时间状语，意为"当处于对话中时"，无陷阱。
【定位】 P1 We all tend to subconsciously copy gestures of people we like. 我们都会下意识地模仿自己喜欢之人的手势。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Repeat what their partners say one way or another 把原文的 copy gestures（模仿动作）偷换成 Repeat what...say（重复话语），原文谈的是肢体动作而非言语内容。 B) 答非所问 Focus as much as possible on topics of mutual interest 是第二段 The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both 的同义改写，属于 52 题的话题范围，与 51 题问的"做什么"无关。 C) ✓ 正确 subconsciously copy gestures ↔ Imitate their partners' gestures without their knowing it C 项同时复现"模仿手势"与"无意识"两个预判要素，且无额外添加成分，与定位句严格等值。 D) 偷换概念 Observe carefully how their partners make use of gestures 把原文动词 copy（模仿）偷换成 Observe（观察）——观察是单方注视、不构成模仿行为，性质完全不同。

records.stem: When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation?

options.text: When both sides are sympathetic with each other.
When both sides have a lot of things in common.
When both sides make interesting contributions.
When both sides try to seek common ground.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation? 用 When 直接问 mirroring 发生的条件，是客观事实题。
【拆句】 When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation? 一般疑问倒装结构，主语 mirroring，谓语 take place，副词 usually 修饰频度；句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】 P2 As a rule, mirroring means that conversationalists enjoy their communication and that there's a certain level of agreement between them. The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both and they know their interests meet. 一般而言，mirroring 意味着对话双方享受彼此的交流，并且双方之间存在一定程度的共识。讨论的话题对双方同样有趣，他们知道彼此兴趣相合。
【选项】 A) 与原文相反 When both sides are sympathetic with each other 利用 not always because the person is sympathetic 制造干扰；原文恰恰说"并非总是因为同情"——A 把这层被否定的说法当成 mirroring 发生的条件，与原文相反。 B) ✓ 正确 there's a certain level of agreement between them. records.stem: Why is the saying "copy from two, it's research" a lesson to learn?

options.text: It facilitates the creation of one's own writing style.
It helps to protect one's intellectual property rights.
It fosters correct interpretation of professional writing.
It enables one to write intriguing sequels to famous stories.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 Why is the saying “copy from two, it's research” a lesson to learn? 用 Why 直接问原文对该格言的解释，不带 infer/imply，按细节题处理。

records.stem: What did Neil Postman say about the rise of television?

【定位】 P1 As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic(印刷的) culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment. 正如尼尔·波兹曼在其 1985 年出版的《娱乐至死》一书中所指出的，电视的兴起带来的不仅是一种新媒介，更是一种新话语：一种从印刷文化到图像文化的渐变，而这又意味着一种从理性到情感、从论述到娱乐的转向。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment ↔ a change from dominance of reason to supremacy of pleasure 预判要求「从理性到娱乐/情感」，a change from dominance of reason to supremacy of pleasure 同时锁住起点 reason 与终点 pleasure，是定位句的标准同义改写。 B) 偷换概念 cinema going to home entertainment 把话题从「理性 vs 娱乐」偷换成「看电影 vs 居家娱乐」，原文从未讨论 cinema going。 C) 偷换概念 a revolution in photographic technology 把原文 typographic(印刷的) culture to a photographic one 中 photographic（图像化的，与 typographic 印刷化相对）误读为「摄影技术」。原文谈的是文化形态而非摄影术革命。 D) 以偏概全 a new age in the entertainment industry 把原文对「娱乐文化全面侵入理性」的批判性论述，矮化为「娱乐产业新时代」这一中性的产业事件，既缩小了范围（仅产业），又抽走了「理性被取代」的核心立场。

It also means to weigh ideas, to compare and contrast assertions, to connect one generalization to another. 正是文本使我们能够识破谎言、混乱与过度概括，发现逻辑与常识被滥用的地方。它还意味着权衡观点、比较与对比断言、把一个概括与另一个概括连接起来。

records.stem: What kind of leaders are viewed as ethical by entitled employees?

options.text: Those who can be counted on to fulfill commitments.

Those who know how to satisfy their employees' needs.

【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What kind of leaders are viewed as ethical by entitled employees? 问哪一类领导被特定群体视为符合某属性，按原文中描述这种被视为关系的句子定位即可。
【拆句】 What kind of leaders are viewed as ethical by entitled employees? 主干 What kind of leaders are viewed as ethical，被动结构 are viewed as，by entitled employees 是动作发出者；结构需注意被动语态的方向：是 "被 entitled employees 视为"，不是反过来。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 The manufacturing sector is declining at a fast rate 称制造业整体在快速衰退，但 Our country is manufacturing more than ever before, but we are doing it with fewer workers 显示制造业产出反而 "前所未有的多"，并非 declining。 B) ✓ 正确 Despite the widespread fears about trade, a recent report showed that just 13 percent of jobs lost in manufacturing are due to trade ↔ The concerns about the effect of trade are exaggerated 把预判 "担忧言过其实" 与四个选项一比，只有 exaggerated 与之同义。 C) 答非所问 The fears about trade have been spreading far and wide 描述的是恐惧本身在扩散，但 P3 报告内容是 "只有 13% 归因于贸易"，并非讲恐惧的传播范围；且 widespread 是状态而非 "正在扩散"。 D) 与原文相反 The impact of trade on employment has been staggering 说贸易对就业影响 "惊人之大"，但 just 13 percent…are due to trade 表明贸易影响极小；staggering 反而是文中用于形容 "statistics in manufacturing" 的词，被错位挪用。

records.stem: What does the author think of automation?

options.text: It will have the same impact as industrialization.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （态度题）
【判型】 What does the author think of automation 直接问作者对自动化的看法，是观点/态度题的标准题干。
【拆句】 What does the author think of automation：主干 the author think of automation，think of 在此意为 "对…的看法"。结构简单，但要小心 think of 是固定短语，等同于 think about / view。
【定位】 P5 I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation's detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical. 我真诚地希望那些断言自动化将让我们更高效、为新职业铺路的人是对的，但自动化对工人的不利影响这一现实让我心存疑虑。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 It will have the same impact as industrialization 称自动化与工业化影响相同；但原文 Resisting automation is futile: it is as inevitable as industrialization was before it 只用 industrialization 作 "不可避免性" 的类比，并未说两者 impact 一样。 B) 张冠李戴 It provides sensible companies with alternatives 说自动化为公司提供备选方案；原文 any sensible company or country should prepare for all alternatives 是公司 "应自己准备好应对各种可能"，主语错位（公司主动准备 → 选项变成自动化提供）。 C) ✓ 正确 I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation's detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical ↔ Its alleged positive effects are doubtful 预判语义 "所谓正面效果不可靠" 与 C 字面几乎一对一对应。 D) 过度推断 Its detrimental effects are unavoidable 称 "不利影响不可避免"；原文 it is as inevitable as industrialization 说的是 "自动化本身不可避免"，被诱导嫁接到 detrimental effects 上；且作者重点是 skeptical（怀疑乐观说法），而非给 detrimental effects 下 "不可避免" 的定论。
records.keyword_relation: I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation's detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical ↔ Its alleged positive effects are doubtful

evidence.text: I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation's detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical

records.stem: What error do experts often make when describing people from other places?

options.text: They tend to overly rely on nationality.
They tend to dwell on national averages.

records.explanation:

【判型】 What error do experts often make when describing people from other places? 是问"什么错误"——指向文中明确陈述的事实，没有 infer/imply 一类词。
【拆句】 Q51 主干是 What error do experts often make（experts 是主语、make 是谓语、error 前移作疑问宾语），后接时间状语从句 when describing people from other places（when + 现在分词，省略 they are）。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】 P1 Yet, when we speak of people from elsewhere, we seem to inevitably characterize them based on their country of origin. 然而，当我们谈论来自他处的人时，我们似乎总是不可避免地根据其原籍国来描述他们。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 characterize them based on their country of origin ↔ overly rely on nationality 预判落在"按国别给外国人贴标签"上，A 选项的 overly rely on nationality 把"按 X 归类 + 不可避免"两层意思干净打包，与预判完全对应。 B) 无中生有 exaggerate their differences 原文从未出现；P1 强调的是"国别概括" vs "个体差异"，不是"夸大"或"缩小"差异。 C) 偷换概念 misunderstand their cultures 把"按国别概括"偷换成"误解文化"；P1 的错误是"贴国别标签"这个动作本身，至于"是否误解了文化内容"，P1 并没有说。 D) 张冠李戴 dwell on national averages 出自 Statistics specialists, when they speak of national averages——national averages 是"统计专家"特有的工具，不是泛指的"专家"在描述"外国人"时的通病。题干虽用 experts，但承接的是 P1 "我们"的归类错误，P2 只是补充统计专家也犯"同一个"错；这个"同一个错"本质是"按国别归类"，而不是"沉迷国家平均值"——national averages 只是统计专家展现这一错误的具体形式。

records.stem: What do we learn about Hofstede's cultural dimensions?

options.text: They are useful in comparing cultural values across time and space.
They have brought unusual benefits to people of different cultures.
They are widely used to identify people's individual traits.
They provide valuable questions for researchers to study.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 What do we learn about Hofstede's cultural dimensions? 问的是关于 X 我们"了解到"什么，指向文中对该术语的客观陈述。
【拆句】 Q52 主干 What do we learn（疑问宾语前移），介词短语 about Hofstede's cultural dimensions 限定话题。结构简单，无陷阱。
【定位】 P4 Though the validity of Hofstede's dimensions has been questioned, they have the singular benefit of having been in use for decades, which allows for historical and international comparisons. 虽然 Hofstede 文化维度的有效性受到过质疑，但它有一个独到的优势——已被使用了数十年，这使得历史性和国际性的比较成为可能。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 allows for historical and international comparisons ↔ useful in comparing cultural values across time and space having been in use for decades ↔ useful 预判与 A 的核心信息在两个维度（时间/空间）和功能（comparing）上一一对应，无多余、无遗漏。 B) 偷换概念 原文说该维度本身 have the singular benefit（"自身具备这一优势"，指研究工具属性），而 brought unusual benefits to people of different cultures 把受益方偷换成"不同文化的人"——文中从未说该维度给"不同文化的人"带来过好处。 C) 与原文相反 identify people's individual traits 与 P4 的 They are not a measure of visible cultural traits, such as food or dress. 不完全冲突，但 P4 明确 Hofstede 维度衡量的是"工作相关的文化价值"，是"群体/文化层面"的 traits，而非"个人特质"。把"群体文化价值"偷换成"个人特质"，方向相反。 D) 无中生有 provide valuable questions for researchers to study 在原文中找不到任何对应——P4 只说该维度本身被研究者使用、能做比较，没说它"提供研究问题"。

records.stem: What did researchers find about previous studies on factors determining people's values?

options.text: Environmental factors were prioritized over other factors.
An individual's financial status was often underestimated.
Too much emphasis had been placed on one's occupation.
The impact of social progress on one's values was ignored.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What did researchers find about previous studies 问"研究者发现了什么"，对应原文 the researchers found that... 一类直接陈述。
【拆句】 Q53 主干 What did researchers find，介词短语 about previous studies on factors determining people's values 三层嵌套：先讲 previous studies，再讲这些研究关于 factors，最后讲这些 factors 是 determining people's values 的。基础薄弱考生易把焦点错认成 previous studies 本身，其实焦点在最里层的 factors。
【定位】 P5 Occupation and social economic status were the most strongly correlated, suggesting that our values are more economically driven than we usually give them credit for. 职业和社会经济地位的相关性最强，这表明我们的价值观更多地是由经济因素驱动的，超出了我们平时给它的认可程度。
【选项】 A) 与原文相反 P5 说 both demographic factors, such as age, and environmental factors, such as long-term unemployment rates, were more correlated with cultural values than nationality——environmental factors 只是"比国籍更相关"的因素之一，且不是"最强"；prioritized over other factors 把它说成"凌驾于其他因素之上"，与"最强相关其实是 occupation 和 social economic status"相反。 B) ✓ 正确 our values are more economically driven than we usually give them credit for ↔ An individual's financial status was often underestimated Occupation and social economic status ↔ An individual's financial status 预判与 B 的两个核心要素"经济维度"和"被低估"都精确对应，无偏。 C) 与原文相反 原文 suggesting that values are more economically driven than we usually give them credit for 表明 occupation/social economic status 一直被"低估"——而 Too much emphasis had been placed on one's occupation 说"过度强调"，方向反转。 D) 无中生有 The impact of social progress on one's values was ignored 中的 social progress 全文未出现；P5 只列了 demographic、environmental、occupation、social economic status 等 factor，没出现 social progress 这个术语。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 fail to see the cultural biases of their business partners 中的"文化偏见"和"看不出"原文均未提及；P7 谈的是"员工被教错了方法"，不是"员工没能识别伙伴的偏见"。 B) 偷换概念 fail to attach sufficient importance to cultural diversity 把考点偷换成"对文化多样性不够重视"——而 P7 谴责的恰恰是"按国家归类时，假定差异（如中国人不够个人主义）"，问题是"错把差异本质化"，而非"忽视多样性"。 C) ✓ 正确 teach their employees useless or even harmful ways of interacting with their international peers ↔ may not be taught how to properly interact with overseas partners "学到无用方式"等于"没学到正确方式"——把同一事实的肯定—正面表述和否定—正面表述对得上，就锁定 C。 D) 无中生有 learn the legal procedures for business transactions 利用 P7 例子里的 Chinese and American lawyers 这一职业关键词，生造出"法律程序"——但律师只是用来举例"中美专业人士因经济地位相似而其实很像"，与"法律程序"无关。

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What is an advantage 问具体的某一项优点，定位到原文表述优点的句子即可，属细节题。
【拆句】 主干 What is an advantage of providing financial aid for students，of 短语限定 advantage 的所属。注意冠词是 an，意为多个优点中的任一个，选项只要原文支持即可，不必是唯一优点。

records.stem: What does the author say about communicating science to the general public?

options.text: It will help them to keep abreast of the latest scientific developments.
It is a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues.

【定位】 P2 Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions. 把科学传播到学术圈外，是增进公众对健康与环境议题理解、帮助个人做出明智决策的必要途径。

records.stem: Why do some people advocate forgiving student loan debt?

options.text: They assert it will narrow the gap between the wealthy and the poor.
They believe it will benefit both the economy and the underprivileged.
They claim it will eliminate economic distress among college students.
They think the cost of education is the responsibility of the government.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 Why do some people advocate forgiving student loan debt? 直接问 "为何主张"，要求回原文找其陈述的理由，属事实陈述题。
【拆句】 题干为标准 Why 引导的特殊疑问句，主谓宾结构清晰：主语 some people，谓语 advocate，宾语动名词短语 forgiving student loan debt，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。
【定位】 P1 Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need. 美国一些人主张：免除学生贷款债务是刺激经济、为困难人群提供援助的一种方式。
【选项】 A) 过度推断 原文只说 give assistance to those in need，并未说 narrow the gap between the wealthy and the poor——"帮助困难者" 不等于 "缩小贫富差距"。 B) ✓ 正确 stimulate the economy ↔ benefit ... the economy give assistance to those in need ↔ benefit ... the underprivileged 预判要求同时覆盖 "经济" 与 "弱势群体"，B 用 both the economy and the underprivileged 并列结构精准对应定位句的并列宾语，是唯一双满足项。 C) 偷换概念 原文 economically distressed 只是 "被免债 1 万美元" 的资格描述，并未声称免债能 eliminate economic distress among college students。 D) 无中生有 原文未出现 the cost of education is the responsibility of the government 这一表述，主张方只谈 "免债" 这一具体动作，未上升到 "教育成本应由政府承担" 的责任归属。
records.keyword_relation: stimulate the economy ↔ benefit ... the economy；give assistance to those in need ↔ benefit ... the underprivileged

evidence.text: Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need

records.stem: What do we learn from the Federal Reserve data?

【拆句】 Wh- 疑问句，what 作宾语前置，"learn from" 为搭配，from 后接信息来源；句式简洁无修饰。
【定位】 P2 This policy is just giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance. Federal Reserve data reveals that the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt, while the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent. 该政策不过是把钱白送给大学和在读的最富有学生。美联储数据显示：收入最高的 40% 家庭欠下了大约 60% 的未偿学贷，而收入最低的 40% 仅欠不到 20%。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 原文 60% 指 outstanding student debt 中由高收入家庭持有的比例，并非 Approximately 60% of student debt remains unpaid——"未偿" 在原文里是 outstanding（仍欠着），但 60% 修饰的是高收入家庭占比而非未偿率。 B) ✓ 正确 giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance ↔ Cancelling student debt benefits wealthy families most the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt ↔ wealthy families 数据要证明 "消债是给富人送钱"，B 把这一结论用 benefits wealthy families most 复述，是唯一锁定 "受益者方向" 的选项。 C) 与原文相反 原文 giving money away to universities 明示大学正是免债的受益方，C 项却说 Forgiving student debt provides little benefit to universities，与原文截然相反。 D) 与原文相反 原文 the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent 明确说低收入家庭只欠不到 20%，D 项称 Low-income families owe the biggest amount of student debt，方向完全反向。

【拆句】 复合疑问句：主句 What does the author say，宾语从句 students are likely to do，后跟条件状语从句 if they know they needn't repay their loans；需把 if-从句视为情景前提。

records.stem: What will happen if any of the proposed student debt plans is implemented?

options.text: Plumbers and retail workers will have a chance of becoming professionals.

A growing number of students will be able to earn degrees in medicine and law.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 What will happen if any of the proposed student debt plans is implemented? 问方案实施后的结果，原文有对应客观陈述句即可作答。

records.stem: What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule?

options.text: It has met more and more resistance from parents.
It has proved helpful to children's healthy growth.
It confuses parents with regard to kids' education.
It has been discarded in line with recent research.

records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule? 指向一个具体规则的现状/命运，不含 infer/imply/mainly about，属于围绕特定对象核对事实的典型细节题。
【拆句】 题干主干 What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule，是 learn about + 对象的常规疑问句；引号内的 No screens under 2 是省略 be 动词的口号式标题，全句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】 P2 As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window. 从今天起，那条规则已被扔出窗外（即被彻底弃用）。
【选项】 A) 无中生有 met more and more resistance from parents 在原文中找不到对应；rule that most parents cling to 反而显示家长一直紧抱旧规则，与"抵制"相反。 B) 无中生有 proved helpful to children's healthy growth 在原文中无对应；原文只是说家长一直奉行该规则，并未给出"该规则被证明对孩子健康有益"的证据。 C) 张冠李戴 confuses parents with regard to kids' education 把"令家长困惑"扣在旧规则头上；但原文 in the confusing, fast-changing world of kids and media 中 confusing 形容的是"kids and media 这个世界"，不是 No screens under 2 这条规则——这是典型的张冠李戴。 D) ✓ 正确 that rule has been thrown out the window ↔ It has been discarded extensively updated and revised its guidelines... to reflect new research ↔ in line with recent research 预判落点"被弃用/依据新研究"两个要素，正好分别对应 discarded 与 in line with recent research，D 是定位句与紧邻背景句的整合同义替换。

records.stem: What do the new AAP guidelines advocate?

options.text: Young children should be accompanied by parents during screen time.
Parents should be emotionally involved in their children's upbringing.
Young children should watch videos carefully selected by parents.
Parents should protect their children from too much media exposure.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （主旨题）
【判型】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 不指向某一条具体规则，而是问 new AAP guidelines 整体在主张什么，需要把全文若干段拼起来才能回答，属于局部主旨题。
【拆句】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 是 what 作宾语的常规疑问句，主语 new AAP guidelines、谓语 advocate；唯一需要留意 advocate 的语义指向"主张/提倡"，不是"批评/警示"。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 if and only if parents are watching alongside them ↔ accompanied by parents during screen time Co-view with your children ↔ accompanied by parents during screen time they want care-givers to take part in screen time ↔ accompanied by parents during screen time 预判要点"父母陪同孩子用屏"在 P7 P9 至少三处同义表述同时成立，A 项一句话覆盖这条主线，是新指南的整体主张。 B) 过度推断 emotionally involved in their children's upbringing 把范围从"屏幕时间陪伴"扩到"整体育儿过程"；本文限定话题在"屏幕/媒体使用"，不涉及通用育儿建议。 C) 与原文相反 videos carefully selected by parents 强调父母"挑选视频内容"，与 shift the focus from WHAT is on the screen to WHO else is in the room 明确告示的方向相反——新指南要的是 WHO（有谁陪），不是 WHAT（挑什么内容）。 D) 以偏概全 protect their children from too much media exposure 偏向"控制屏幕时间总量"，确实贴近 P8 与 P9 的"一小时上限/避免独看"，但只是 P9 的局部要点之一；它没覆盖贯穿全文的 co-view 主线，作为整体主张以偏概全。

records.stem: What do families think of live video chat according to surveys?

options.text: It should not be regarded as screen time.
It helps babies to develop their verbal skills.
It is not as harmful as playing games on laptops.
It is a good substitute for video viewing.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What do families think of live video chat according to surveys? 指向一句调查结论，答案落在原文一两句话里，是典型细节题。
【拆句】 题干 What do families think of live video chat according to surveys? 主干为 What do families think of...，think of = "对……怎么看"；尾部 according to surveys 是状语，限定信息来源，不是 think 的宾语。
【定位】 P5 Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that "Face time doesn't count", or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone. 调查显示，许多家庭已经普遍相信"视频聊天不算（屏幕时间）"，或者至少认为与祖父母等亲属虚拟相见的好处大于让婴儿接触电脑或智能手机的潜在代价。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 "Face time doesn't count" ↔ It should not be regarded as screen time 预判落点是"家庭把视频聊天排除在屏幕时间之外"，A 恰好是这句话的书面化、完整化版本，是定位句的标准同义替换。 B) 张冠李戴 原文 P5 没有说视频聊天帮助婴儿"发展语言能力"；emotionally engaged 给出的也是"情感投入"而非语言；P7 谈到 learn new words 但前提是 educational media+父母伴看，与 live video chat 是不同话题。 C) 无中生有 not as harmful as playing games on laptops 把视频聊天与"在笔记本上玩游戏"作比较，但原文 P5 只比较"虚拟探访的好处"与"接触手机的潜在代价"，从未把 video chat 与 playing games 放一起比较。 D) 无中生有 a good substitute for video viewing 把视频聊天说成"看视频的好替代品"，但 P5 只说家庭认为视频聊天"不算屏幕时间"，并未在视频聊天与看视频之间建立替代关系。

records.stem: What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos?

options.text: It arouses their interest in language learning.
It works no better than reading picture books.
It hampers their development of language skills.
It helps them acquire independent learning skills.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos? 指向一句研究结论，是典型细节题。
【拆句】 题干 What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos? 主干 What do researchers find about X；about 的宾语 kids solo viewing educational videos 是"动名词复合结构"——solo viewing 作动名词中心，前面 kids 是逻辑主语，相当于"孩子独自观看教育视频"这一行为。
【定位】 P8 The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos. 另一方面，许多研究实际上已经表明，过早地独自观看"教育"视频与较差的语言能力相关。
【选项】 A) 与原文相反 arouses their interest in language learning 原文未提兴趣，且原文方向是"独看伴随更差语言能力"，与"激发兴趣"方向相反。 B) 偷换概念 works no better than reading picture books 把 treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet 错读为"二者效果一样"；原文是"把视频当绘本来读才是最佳做法"，并未说"独看视频和读绘本一样"。 C) ✓ 正确 poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos ↔ It hampers their development of language skills 原文 poorer skills correlated with solo viewing 等同于"独看与语言能力变差相关"，C 的 hampers 正是这一负向相关的动词化表达。 D) 无中生有 helps them acquire independent learning skills 把"独看"硬扯成"获得自主学习能力"；原文不仅未提及自主学习，反而把 solo 与负向后果绑定。

evidence.text: The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos

distractor_explanations.A: 与原文相反：arouses their interest in language learning 原文未提兴趣，且原文方向是"独看伴随更差语言能力"，与"激发兴趣"方向相反。
distractor_explanations.B: 偷换概念：works no better than reading picture books 把 treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet 错读为"二者效果一样"；原文是"把视频当绘本来读才是最佳做法"，并未说"独看视频和读绘本一样"。

records.stem: What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5?

options.text: They can understand pretty well what they see on the screen.
They can learn on their own without much parental guidance.
They can make use of educational videos to develop digital literacy.
They can relate what they learn on the screen to real life situations.

records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5? 指向作者对一个具体人群的具体陈述，可在某一段内得到完整答案，是细节题。
【拆句】 题干 What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5? 主干 What does the author say about X；ages 2 to 5 是 preschoolers 的同位修饰语，等价于 who are 2 to 5 years old，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】 P9 For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math. 对于 2 到 5 岁的学龄前儿童而言，有更多证据表明他们能够把从屏幕上学到的知识迁移到现实世界，包括早期识字与数学能力。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 understand pretty well what they see on the screen 与原文 help children understand what they are seeing 中的"理解"措辞相近，但原文这句是 AAP 对父母的"建议"——要父母帮孩子理解，并非"孩子已经能理解"的事实结论。 B) 与原文相反 learn on their own without much parental guidance 与原文 they want care-givers to take part in screen time 直接相反——原文强调要父母参与，B 项说不需要父母指导。 C) 偷换概念 develop digital literacy 把原文 early literacy and math 中的"早期识字"偷换为"数字素养"——early literacy 指儿童的识字、阅读能力，与 digital literacy（数字素养/媒介使用能力）不是一回事。 D) ✓ 正确 transfer knowledge from screens to the real world ↔ relate what they learn on the screen to real life situations 预判要点"屏上所学应用到现实"，D 用 relate to real life situations 准确还原 transfer to the real world，是定位句的同义替换。
records.keyword_relation: transfer knowledge from screens to the real world ↔ relate what they learn on the screen to real life situations

evidence.text: For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math

distractor_explanations.B: 与原文相反：learn on their own without much parental guidance 与原文 they want care-givers to take part in screen time 直接相反——原文强调要父母参与，B 项说不需要父母指导。
distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：develop digital literacy 把原文 early literacy and math 中的"早期识字"偷换为"数字素养"——early literacy 指儿童的识字、阅读能力，与 digital literacy（数字素养/媒介使用能力）不是一回事。

【答案】 K) released 动词
【词性槽】 「a report ___ yesterday」report 后修饰、yesterday 锁过去时 → 过去分词作后置定语
【依据】 release a report = 发布报告，是固定搭配 said in a report __(26)__ yesterday 中 release a report（发布报告）是新闻语篇里的典型搭配，与「EIA 昨天发布的一份报告里说……」语义完全咬合。
【竞争词】 G) mobilized mobilize a report 不通 mobilize 与「人力、资源、军队」搭，从不修饰 report；语义上「动员一份报告」也讲不通。

records.stem: 选择第 27 空的词汇
records.explanation:
【答案】 A) abandoned 动词
【词性槽】 「have ___ coal completely」现在完成时缺过去分词
【依据】 「彻底放弃燃煤」与全文「减煤」主线完全吻合 20 have __(27)__ coal completely 与 American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago 形成程度递进——大多数学校少用，20 所「彻底放弃」。abandon coal 是脱煤议题的高频表达。
【竞争词】 G) mobilized 「动员了煤炭」与「停用煤炭」方向相反 mobilize 意为「动员、调动」，have mobilized coal completely 等于「已经把煤完全动员起来用」，与「彻底放弃」截然相反，逻辑错位。 K) released release coal 不通且与上下文矛盾 release coal 不是常用搭配（release 多与 report、information、emissions 搭），且与「使用」无关；后续 26 题更需要 released 来搭配 report，此处不应抢用。
【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— released 词性形态都对，最易抢走 27 题 。have ___ coal completely 处 K)released 形态完全合规，且 release 在新闻语体里高频；但 release coal 不是自然搭配，且 26 题 a report ___ yesterday 才是 released 的归属。考生若不按「先易后难、用过即划」的顺序，容易把 K 提前用到 27 题、导致 26 题再也找不到合适的过去分词。防坑：先做 26 题（因为 a report released yesterday 的搭配更硬），把 K 划走，27 题就自然落到 abandoned 上。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the differences between people's rates of aging ↔ Why people age at different rates it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists ↔ come to know better 预判"为何人们衰老速度不同"与Why people age at different rates逐词同义对应，且A完整覆盖了定位句的核心信息（差异+原因）。 B) 过度推断 定位句只说"差异源于基因等多因素互动"，并未具体阐述"基因如何影响衰老过程"；选项How genes influence the aging process问的是机制原理，是原文没展开的内容。 C) 无中生有 定位句只点名"基因等因素互动"，原文Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves.虽提到基因表达，但并未说"各种基因如何在衰老中表达自己"——选项C说的various genes在衰老中"各自如何表达"原文未有此层级讨论。 D) 答非所问 Why people have long been concerned about aging问的是"人们为何长期关注衰老"，对应原文Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years提到的"已问数千年"——但这是背景，不是"科学家最近搞清楚的事"，与题干come to know better today错位。

records.stem: What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme scientists have created?

options.text: It was identified during a lab experiment accident.
It may make full recycling of plastic bottles a reality.
It was a breakthrough made with persistent efforts.
It may initiate a radical reform in plastic industry.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme scientists have created? 是 What do we learn about X 的标准客观陈述问法，不含 infer / imply，不问 main idea / attitude，属细节题。
【拆句】 题干主干为 What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme，about 引导的介词短语限定 learn 的对象；其后 scientists have created 是省略 that 的定语从句修饰 enzyme，结构清晰，无陷阱。
【定位】 P1 The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles. 这一突破有望首次实现塑料瓶的完全回收，从而帮助解决全球塑料污染危机。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 identified during a lab experiment accident 偷换了原文 created by accident——原文意思是"偶然创造出"，A 项却说成"在一次实验事故中被识别（identified）出来"，identified（识别）≠ created（创造），且 lab experiment accident（实验事故）也无原文支撑。 B) ✓ 正确 enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles ↔ may make full recycling of plastic bottles a reality the full recycling of bottles ↔ full recycling of plastic bottles B 项既覆盖"完全回收"又保留"可能性"语气，与定位句 could help…by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles 严格对应，是定位句的同义改写。 C) 与原文相反 breakthrough made with persistent efforts 与原文 created by accident 直接相反；同段还点明 a bit of a shock 进一步坐实"意外性"。 D) 无中生有 initiate a radical reform in plastic industry 中的 radical reform（根本性改革）在原文中无任何对应句；原文谈的是"帮助解决污染"和"完全回收"，并未谈及行业改革。
records.keyword_relation: enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles ↔ may make full recycling of plastic bottles a reality；the full recycling of bottles ↔ full recycling of plastic bottles

evidence.text: The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles

records.stem: What does the passage say about the bug that produces the important enzyme?

options.text: It has a natural ability to consume plastics.
It is a bacterium that reproduces at a high rate.
It is essential to the recycling of plastic bottles.
It has a chemical structure unknown to scientists.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What does the passage say about the bug that produces the important enzyme? 用 say about 直接索取原文对 the bug 的客观陈述，不含推断词，属细节题。
【拆句】 the bug that produces the important enzyme 中 that 引导的定语从句修饰 bug；六级考生需看清 produces 的主语是 the bug 而非更靠近的 enzyme，即所问对象是 bug 本身的特征。
【定位】 P2 The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan. 这项新研究的契机是 2016 年在日本一处垃圾场发现的首个自然进化出能吃塑料能力的细菌。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 naturally evolved to eat plastic ↔ natural ability to consume plastics A 项把定位句的动词陈述（自然进化出去吃塑料）改写为名词陈述（具有自然消化塑料的能力），是该细菌核心特征的客观转述。 B) 无中生有 reproduces at a high rate（高速繁殖）在原文中没有任何对应句；原文只说该细菌"自然进化"且"吃塑料"，没有谈论其繁殖速度。 C) 偷换概念 essential to the recycling of plastic bottles 把所问对象（bug 本身的属性）偷换成"对回收的必要性"——这是对其衍生用途的评价，而非对 bug 本身的描述；且原文也未声称 bug 对回收"必不可少"。 D) 与原文相反 chemical structure unknown to scientists 与原文 Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug. 相反；原文明确"已揭示详细结构"，选项却说"科学家不知道"。

evidence.text: The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan

records.stem: By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______.

options.text: made it more effective by chance
found its evolutionary process sped up

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 题干是不完整陈述 By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______.，要选项补全，问的是科学家做了什么的客观结果，不含推断动词。
【拆句】 By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______. 主干是 the scientists ____；By 引导方式状语，produced by the bug 是过去分词短语后置定语修饰 enzyme，结构清晰。
【定位】 P3 An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles. 国际团队随后调整了该酶以观察其进化过程，但实验表明他们意外地让这一分子分解饮料瓶塑料的能力变得更强了。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic ↔ made it more effective by chance A 项 made it more effective 复述 even better at breaking down，by chance 复述 accidentally，正好等值改写定位句两个核心要素。 B) 无中生有 discovered an extraordinary chemical 中 extraordinary chemical 在原文无出处；研究者操作的是已知酶分子，并非"发现一种新化学物质"。 C) 过度推断 altered its basic molecular composition 中 basic molecular composition（基本分子组成）属于结构层级更深的概念，原文只说 adjusted the enzyme（调整酶），未说改变其"基本组成"。 D) 偷换概念 found its evolutionary process sped up 中 sped up（加速）与原文 to see how it had evolved（观察其如何进化）不一致；原文目的是观察，并未发现进化过程被加速。
records.keyword_relation: accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic ↔ made it more effective by chance

distractor_explanations.C: 过度推断：altered its basic molecular composition 中 basic molecular composition（基本分子组成）属于结构层级更深的概念，原文只说 adjusted the enzyme（调整酶），未说改变其"基本组成"。
distractor_explanations.D: 偷换概念：found its evolutionary process sped up 中 sped up（加速）与原文 to see how it had evolved（观察其如何进化）不一致；原文目的是观察，并未发现进化过程被加速。

records.stem: What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles?

options.text: Manufacturers are implementing it on an increasingly larger scale.
It generates huge business opportunities for plastic manufacturers.
It has aroused persistent interest among the general public.
Manufacturers are beginning to explore ways of doing it.

records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles? 索取 McGeehan 关于回收的客观说法，属细节题。
【拆句】 What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles? 标准 Wh- 疑问句，about 短语限定 say 的话题对象，无陷阱。
【定位】 P8 perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles. 公众观念变化如此之大，以至于企业正开始研究如何妥善回收这些瓶子。
【选项】 A) 过度推断 implementing it on an increasingly larger scale 中 implementing on a larger scale（大规模实施）远超 starting to look at（开始研究）的程度——原文是观念转变后的初始阶段，并未谈到任何实施规模。 B) 无中生有 generates huge business opportunities for plastic manufacturers 中 huge business opportunities（巨大商业机会）原文未提；McGeehan 谈的是企业态度转变，不是回收带来的商机。 C) 偷换概念 aroused persistent interest among the general public 中 persistent interest（持续 / 长期兴趣）与原文 perception is changing so much（观念正在巨大变化）不一致——原文说"正在变化"，C 说"已激起且持续"；且讨论对象是公众而非回收行为本身，与题干 about the recycling of plastic bottles 错位。 D) ✓ 正确 companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles ↔ Manufacturers are beginning to explore ways of doing it companies ↔ Manufacturers D 项把"才刚开始"和"探索如何回收"两个核心信息都对齐原文，是定位句的精准同义改写。
records.keyword_relation: companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles ↔ Manufacturers are beginning to explore ways of doing it；companies ↔ Manufacturers

distractor_explanations.A: 过度推断：implementing it on an increasingly larger scale 中 implementing on a larger scale（大规模实施）远超 starting to look at（开始研究）的程度——原文是观念转变后的初始阶段，并未谈到任何实施规模。
distractor_explanations.B: 无中生有：generates huge business opportunities for plastic manufacturers 中 huge business opportunities（巨大商业机会）原文未提；McGeehan 谈的是企业态度转变，不是回收带来的商机。
distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：aroused persistent interest among the general public 中 persistent interest（持续 / 长期兴趣）与原文 perception is changing so much（观念正在巨大变化）不一致——原文说"正在变化"，C 说"已激起且持续"；且讨论对象是公众而非回收行为本身，与题干 about the recycling of plastic bottles 错位。

records.stem: What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme?

options.text: Developing technologies to address greenhouse gas emissions.
Considering the extra cost involved in producing the enzyme.
Assessing its possible negative impact on the environment.
Studying the full life cycle of the enzyme as the first step.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme? 索取该专家的具体建议，属细节题。
【拆句】 What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme? 中 concerning the application of the enzyme 是介词短语修饰 advice，limit 范围为"针对酶的应用"，结构清晰。
【定位】 P9 A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions. 需要进行一次完整的生命周期评估，以确保该技术不会以制造其他环境问题（包括额外的温室气体排放）为代价来解决一个环境问题（废弃物）。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Developing technologies to address greenhouse gas emissions 中 developing technologies 与原文 assessment（评估）不同——原文建议"评估"，并非"开发新技术"去解决排放问题。 B) 无中生有 Considering the extra cost involved in producing the enzyme 中 extra cost in producing the enzyme（生产酶的额外成本）原文无出处；Adisa Azapagic 的建议是评估环境影响而非经济成本。 C) ✓ 正确 does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions ↔ Assessing its possible negative impact on the environment A full life-cycle assessment would be needed ↔ Assessing C 项的 Assessing 对应 assessment，possible negative impact on the environment 对应 not solve…at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions；正答完整覆盖建议的两个语义要点。 D) 偷换概念 Studying the full life cycle of the enzyme as the first step 中 the full life cycle of the enzyme（酶本身的生命周期）与原文 A full life-cycle assessment（针对技术应用的全生命周期评估）所指不同——原文评估的是技术对环境的全周期影响，并非"酶的寿命周期"；另外 as the first step（作为第一步）原文亦无对应。

records.stem: 选择第 26 空的词汇
records.explanation:
【答案】 N) surpass 动词
【词性槽】 does not 后接动词原形
【依据】 “并不超过其他聪明动物”照应主旨 前句说 dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores(食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals，下半句用 but 转折，意思必然是“但并不在这些类别里 X 其他聪明动物”。surpass 表“超过、胜过”，正合“狗虽聪明但并未超越同类”的论断，与第二段 their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed 互相印证。
【竞争词】 D) differentiate “区分”后通常接 between/from differentiate 表“区分”，差异辨别义，与 intelligence does not differentiate other animals 搭不上；且 D 另有去处（见 32 题“辨别人声”）。 J) pledge “保证”不接动物作宾 pledge 表“承诺、保证”，主语必须是人或机构，intelligence 作主语不能 pledge animals，语义彻底错位。 M) prove “证明其他动物”逻辑断裂 prove 后通常接 that 从句或形容词补足语；intelligence does not prove other animals 不构成完整意思，且 M 另有去处（见 29 题）。
【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— outperformed 词义近、形态却错 。outperformed 意为“胜过”，词义几乎与 surpass 一致，最容易被误选进 their intelligence does not __(26)__ other intelligent animals。一句话防坑：does not 后必跟动词原形，outperformed 是过去分词/过去式，词形先被淘汰。
records.keyword_relation: “并不超过其他聪明动物”照应主旨

evidence.text: Scientists recently examined studies on dog intelligence and compared them with research into the minds of other intelligent animals. The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores(食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not  {{26}}  other intelligent animals in any of those categories. Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition  {{27}}  , the authors of this new study found little to warrant the  {{28}}  of work that has been devoted to the topic.

distractor_explanations.D: “区分”后通常接 between/from：differentiate 表“区分”，差异辨别义，与 intelligence does not differentiate other animals 搭不上；且 D 另有去处（见 32 题“辨别人声”）。
distractor_explanations.J: “保证”不接动物作宾：pledge 表“承诺、保证”，主语必须是人或机构，intelligence 作主语不能 pledge animals，语义彻底错位。
distractor_explanations.M: “证明其他动物”逻辑断裂：prove 后通常接 that 从句或形容词补足语；intelligence does not prove other animals 不构成完整意思，且 M 另有去处（见 29 题）。

records.stem: 选择第 28 空的词汇
records.explanation:
【答案】 O) volume 名词
【词性槽】 the 与 of 短语之间的名词中心词
【依据】 “工作量之多”才能被 warrant 衡量 warrant 意为“证明…是必要/正当的”，宾语应是某种可被衡量的“量”。volume 表“数量、规模”，the volume of work 即“工作量”，承接前文 Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __(27)__ 中的 a significant body of research，呼应“研究量之大是否值得”的主线，是全文论点的关键词。
【竞争词】 F) domain “工作领域”与 warrant 搭不上 domain 表“领域”，the domain of work 听上去是“工作的领域”，但 warrant the domain of work（证明这一工作领域的合理性）逻辑别扭，且与下文“量”的比较主题不符。

records.stem: What is the consequence of algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment?

options.text: People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.

Managers no longer have the chance to decide which loan to approve.
Managers do not need to take the trouble to determine who to hire or fire.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 What is the consequence of …是问某行为带来的具体后果，答案在原文有明确对应句而非需推断。
【拆句】 Q47结构清晰：主干what is the consequence of X，of后接动名词短语algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment，其中replacing为现在分词作定语修饰prescription，相当于"算法处方替代了人的判断"。
【定位】 P4 These are areas where algorithmic prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will. 这些就是算法处方正在取代人类判断的领域，因此本来可能有机会在这些领域培养实践判断力的人，不再有此机会。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will ↔ People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments. 预判正是"失去培养判断力的机会"，People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.逐字对应。 B) 偷换概念 原文是"失去培养判断力的练习机会"，B把它偷换成"被阻止参与重大决策"——重大决策的参与权并未被剥夺，被剥夺的是"练手"机会。 C) 张冠李戴 原文说被剥夺机会的是普通人（people），不是经理（managers）；经理本是行使判断的一方，正被算法替代。 D) 与原文相反 原文是中性陈述"经理们日常会做这些决定"，并未说他们觉得麻烦或希望被替代；D把负面后果"失去机会"扭曲成正面"省事"。

records.stem: What may result from increasing application of recommendation engines in our consumption of culture?

options.text: Consumers will have much limited choice.

records.explanation:

【判型】 What may result from …直接问由某事导致的具体结果，是典型的细节题问法。
【拆句】 Q48主干what may result from X，may弱化了语气表"可能性"，X是动名词短语increasing application of recommendation engines in our consumption of culture，其中increasing修饰application，整体意为"推荐引擎在文化消费里日益增多的应用"。
【定位】 P5 Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. 推荐引擎在人们的文化消费中日益普遍地充当中介，可能会限制选择、削减偶然。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck ↔ Consumers will have much limited choice. 预判"限制选择"，Consumers will have much limited choice.恰是其形容词化版本，正面对应。 B) 与原文相反 原文是minimize luck（削减偶然/运气），B却说"享受更好的运气"——意思完全反向。 C) 以偏概全 原文中"机器能扫描更广范围"只是让步性铺垫（"In one sense, this is helpful"），紧接P6"At the same time, though"明确转折，作者的核心结论是限制选择，而不是"决定更容易"。 D) 偷换概念 原文是"用机器口味替代人的口味"（machine taste replaces human taste），即人的口味被压制；D却说"人将培养出与机器相似的口味"，主客体反了。

【判型】 What is likely to happen to … as …是问条件下将发生的具体情况，找原文对应预测句即可。
【拆句】 Q49结构是"What is likely to happen to A as B"，as引导时间/条件状语从句，意为"随着B，A身上可能发生什么"；考生易把as误读为"因为"，这里其实更接近"随着"。

records.stem: Why does the author say the creatures living in the more and more AI-mediated world will become increasingly unlike us?

【定位】 P9 But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us. 但是，由于不可预测性本身就是人类自我认知与自我喜爱的一部分，人类正在失去某种重要的东西。随着他们变得越来越可预测，居住在愈发AI化的世界里的这些"生物"，将越来越不像我们。

As they become more and more predictable ↔ They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable. 预判核心词是unpredictability，四个选项中只有They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable.点出unpredictable，正面命中。 C) 过度推断 原文说unpredictability是"how people understand themselves"的一部分，并没有说"未来人将无法理解自己"——C把作为成分的unpredictability当成了理解能力本身。 D) 以偏概全 D只说"被剥夺了前人曾为之自豪的东西"——但"前人曾为之自豪的东西"具体是什么，D避而不答；正确答案B则点明那就是unpredictability。Why题要的是具体原因，不是含糊代称。

As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us

【拆句】 What has America been witnessing for decades? 主干 America has been witnessing what，for decades 是持续性时间状语，与现在完成进行时呼应。
【定位】 P3 America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. 美国陷入了一场关于如何教孩子阅读的争论，这场争论已经持续了几十年。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading. 把核心从 "争论" 偷换成 "对创新阅读教学法的痴迷"，原文谈的是两派持续对立而非痴迷创新。 B) ✓ 正确 a debate about teaching children to read ↔ An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read. has been going on for decades ↔ enduring B 项把定位句里 "持续数十年" + "关于教孩子阅读的争论" 两个核心元素分别压缩为 enduring + debate over the approach to teaching children to read，与预判精准对应。 C) 偷换概念 An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy. 把对象换成 "对许多孩子识字不足的担忧"，原文 P2 提到识字率低只是后果数据，并不是 "美国数十年来一直在见证" 的主体。 D) 与原文相反 An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading. 说 "对组合法越来越有力的倡导"，但原文明确通过 Tenette Smith 说 This combination of methods is ineffective，与选项方向相反。

records.stem: Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____.

options.text: life-long consumerism is causing more and more cases of psychological problems.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____. 是不完整陈述句，要求选项填入研究的内容，等同于追问该研究的结论事实，归为细节题。
【拆句】 主句 Many child development experts and educators call attention to research，that suggests 后续宾语从句由选项补齐；call attention to＝呼吁关注，是熟词僻义提醒，主语动作就是「指出研究表明……」。
【定位】 P4 Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness. 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育者援引研究指出：这种正在出现的「从摇篮到坟墓」的消费主义，正在导致低自尊、抑郁和其他形式心理疾病的发生率不断上升。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism ↔ life-long consumerism growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness ↔ more and more cases of psychological problems is contributing to ↔ is causing 选项 A 的主语「终生消费主义」、谓语「正在导致」、宾语「越来越多心理问题」与定位句三项要点逐一同义对应，是最精确的复述。 B) 无中生有 increasing commercialization of education 在原文中完全没有提及，作者批评的是面向孩子的广告与营销，不是教育自身的商业化。 C) 以偏概全 the growing desire for wealth 只是原文 fame and wealth 的一半；a rising rate of depression 也只是 low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness 的一项。两处都只取了原文的局部。 D) 答非所问 the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life 说的是「物欲是如何被培养起来的」，而题干要求复述「研究表明的因果结论」——D 项把因果关系换成了「物欲是如何形成」，与题干追问方向不一致。

evidence.text: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness

distractor_explanations.C: 以偏概全：the growing desire for wealth 只是原文 fame and wealth 的一半；a rising rate of depression 也只是 low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness 的一项。两处都只取了原文的局部。

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （推断题）
【判型】 What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 中的 imply 表明本题要求基于原文作推断，而非复述事实。
【拆句】 What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 主干是 What ... the author imply，about the impact of advertising 限定推断对象；句子简洁，需注意 imply 是「暗示」而非「明示」。
【定位】 P5 It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. 它（广告业）也是这样一个行业：不断开发新方法来诱使我们的孩子渴望物质；而由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需感染少数即可触及多数。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 they only need to infect a few to reach the many ↔ It is actually infectious to many rather than a few they only need to infect a few to reach the many ↔ rather than a few 由 infect a few to reach the many 一步推出「广告其实波及多数而非少数」，正好是 imply 题所要的「一步推断」型答案。 B) 与原文相反 rooted in our desire for material possessions 把因果反过来——原文是「广告诱使孩子产生物欲」（persuade our children to desire material possessions），不是「广告源于物欲」。 C) 过度推断 comparable to that of virus 已经超出原文 viral effect 的比喻：原文只说「影响具有病毒式扩散效应」，并没断言「广告影响可与病毒影响相提并论」。两者程度差异明显。 D) 与原文相反 literally limited to children 把广告影响范围缩限到「仅限于儿童」，而原文 infect a few to reach the many 恰恰强调影响会扩散到「多数」，并非「仅限于儿童」。

evidence.text: It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many

records.stem: What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children?

options.text: It would deprive them of the chance to learn about products.
It would render them unable to carve out unique identities.
It would breach their freedom as would-be consumers.
It would violate the rights endowed upon advertisers.

records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children? 直接问反对者给出的具体论据，对应原文中已写明的让步句，属细节题。
【拆句】 主干 What is the opponents' argument，against a complete ban on advertising to young children 是后置修饰，整体含义是「反对者反对彻底禁广告时给出的理由」；注意 against 修饰的是 argument，而非整个句子的否定。
【定位】 P7 There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products. 会有人辩称（禁止广告）将构成对言论自由的侵犯，并损害企业「向幼儿洗脑、让他们索要产品」的权利。
【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 deprive them of the chance to learn about products 取自 Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products，是作者描述广告「益处」的内容，并非 P7 中的反方论据。 B) 张冠李戴 render them unable to carve out unique identities 同样取自 help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood，是广告作为「益处」的功能描述，非 P7 中反方对禁令的反对理由。 C) 偷换概念 breach their freedom as would-be consumers 中 their 指 young children；但 a breach of freedom of speech 中被侵犯的是「言论自由」，主语暗指「企业表达自由」，不是「孩子作为准消费者的自由」。 D) ✓ 正确 infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products ↔ violate the rights endowed upon advertisers the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products ↔ the rights endowed upon advertisers 反方第二条论据「损害企业的权利」被选项 D 完整同义改写为「侵犯广告商被赋予的权利」，且两条论据中只有该条被选项明确复述。
records.keyword_relation: infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products ↔ violate the rights endowed upon advertisers；the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products ↔ the rights endowed upon advertisers

evidence.text: There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products

distractor_explanations.B: 张冠李戴：render them unable to carve out unique identities 同样取自 help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood，是广告作为「益处」的功能描述，非 P7 中反方对禁令的反对理由。
distractor_explanations.C: 偷换概念：breach their freedom as would-be consumers 中 their 指 young children；但 a breach of freedom of speech 中被侵犯的是「言论自由」，主语暗指「企业表达自由」，不是「孩子作为准消费者的自由」。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the relentless pressure it brings ↔ puts workers under constant pressure 预判中"持续压力"一条被A项constant pressure逐词同义对应,A为定位句两项理由之一的精确改写,在四个选项中是唯一与原文有同义映射的项。 B) 过度推断 原文说监控具有inherent dehumanizing effect,只是描述其内在属性,并未声称这一点被普遍认同;B项把它升级为universally deemed anti-human,把"内在属性"偷换为"举世公认"。 C) 无中生有 原文只提及dehumanizing effect与relentless pressure,均偏心理与人格层面;C项添加physical harm,原文无任何关于身体伤害的表述。 D) 答非所问 squeeze maximal productivity复述的是企业立场——原文firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers是企业实施监控的动机,而非员工反对的理由,角色彻底错位。

distractor_explanations.C: 无中生有：原文只提及dehumanizing effect与relentless pressure,均偏心理与人格层面;C项添加physical harm,原文无任何关于身体伤害的表述。

【判型】 In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes? 问的是一个明确的可比关系，答案应能从原文一句话直接读出。
【拆句】 主干 does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes，从句 that 省略，理解关键是 comparable to 的语义"与……可比"，不是"被比作"。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 engineered to hook you ↔ addictive not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances ↔ They are all addictive. 预判"勾住人"对应 addictive，A 即为对定位句双重否定+动词短语的整体重述。 B) 无中生有 necessary evils 原文未提及；Moss 全文批评加工食品，没有任何"必要"评价。 C) 偷换概念 engineered to be enjoyed 把原文 engineered to hook you 偷换为"为享受而设计"——hook 是"勾住、使上瘾"的强迫语义，与"被享受"的中性愉悦语义不等。 D) 偷换概念 increasingly great demand 原文未提及"需求日益增大"；Moss 说的是公司在"积极推销"（aggressive marketing），不是消费者需求暴涨。

records.stem: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products?

【判型】 What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 问的是公司具体做了什么，是原文动作的同义改写。
【拆句】 What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 中 to capitalize on... 是目的状语；consumers' association with... 是"消费者对……的联想"。结构清晰、无陷阱。
【定位】 P4 Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. 明白这一点之后，食品行业花费大量时间，努力塑造我们对其产品所留存的记忆。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 trying to shape the memories that we have for their products ↔ strive to influence how consumers remember their products 预判的"塑造记忆"与 influence how consumers remember 在动作（塑造/影响）和对象（记忆/如何记住）上双重对应。 B) 过度推断 use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction 把"塑造记忆"曲解为"利用长期记忆推动成瘾"——原文虽然提到 features of addiction，但其语境是说"食物入脑速度快"，并不是把记忆当成瘾工具。 C) 偷换概念 exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible 把动作偷换为"尽早利用记忆"，并嫁接首段 we begin forming memories for food at a really early age 的"早期"细节——但原文说的是"消费者从小开始形成记忆"，不是"公司尽早去利用"。 D) 偷换概念 endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products 把"塑造（shape）"偷换为"查明（find）"——前者是主动改变记忆，后者是被动调查记忆，方向完全相反。

records.stem: What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals?

options.text: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.
They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.
They possess the most outstanding ability to think.
They know how to survive everywhere on earth.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals? 指向文章中给出原因解释的某一句，并非全文主旨，属于细节题。
【拆句】 主干是 What might explain X，其中 X 由动名词短语 humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals 充当 explain 的宾语；不定式般的动名词结构是六级常见考点，注意 humans' 是 having 的逻辑主语，不是 population 的所有格。
【定位】 P3 One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe. 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的纯粹智力赋予了我们一种前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，让人们在迁徙到全球各处时能够创新性地解决棘手难题。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 选项 equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems 用 raw strength 替换原文 raw intelligence，正话反说——文章首段恰恰强调 despite our physical weaknesses，人类身体反而是弱的。 B) 答非所问 They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives 用 animal relatives 把题点引向 Chimpanzees, human beings' closest animal relatives——黑猩猩，但 51 题问的是 largest population of almost all mammals 的原因，原因句在 P3 而非 P1。 C) ✓ 正确 our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box ↔ possess the most outstanding ability to think our big brains ↔ possess 预判已锁定卓越的思考能力，C 选项 possess the most outstanding ability to think 在词面与语义上都与定位句一一对应，是定位句的标准同义替换。 D) 答非所问 They know how to survive everywhere on earth 是 humans have colonized every corner of the globe 的同义改写，但这是现象本身，不是题目所问的解释；题干 What might explain 要的是 原因。

records.stem: What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?

options.text: They are better at innovating solutions.
They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.
They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.

records.explanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）
【判型】 题干 according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists 限定了观点来源，要求回原文找到该群体说了什么，属典型署名细节题。
【拆句】 主干 What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes，后接 according to 短语作状语限定信息来源；account for 在此意为解释/导致，是六级高频熟词僻义。
【定位】 P4 They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others. 他们认为：我们之所以存活下来并蓬勃发展，恰恰不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而恰恰是因为我们不自己思考。相反，人类是通过仔细地模仿他人来应对极具挑战的气候与生态环境的。
【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 They are better at innovating solutions 来自 innovating solutions to thorny problems——但这是 P4 But 转折之前被驳的旧解释，不是 a growing number of 科学家的观点；题干限定了观点出处，必须取转折之后。 B) 与原文相反 They thrive through creative strategies 用 creative——这与 we don't think for ourselves 直接相反，文章明确说人类成功不靠自己思考创新。 C) 无中生有 They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts 把 ecological contexts 抄过来制造熟悉感，但 naturally adaptive（与生俱来的适应性）这种说法在原文没有任何出处——文章强调的是后天模仿。 D) ✓ 正确 by carefully copying others ↔ imitating others carefully cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts ↔ meet challenges 预判已锁定靠仔细模仿来应对挑战，They meet challenges by imitating others carefully 在结构（meet challenges by + 动名词短语）和措辞上与定位句完全同义。

records.stem: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?

options.text: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.
Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.
Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.
Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 题干问的是作者认为某项研究中 odd 的具体内容，需要回到原文一句话找出对应描述，是细节题而非态度题。
【拆句】 主干 What does the author think is odd about X，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is odd about the findings，about 短语限定 odd 的范围；考生易把 think is odd 误读成主旨态度题。
【定位】 P6 Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed. 奇怪的是，儿童仔细地模仿了开盒子的每一步动作，哪怕他们能看出那根木棒并没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：他们没有只做获得奖励所必需的动作，而是奴隶般地模仿了所看到的每一个动作。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed ↔ Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters every action they'd witnessed ↔ every action of the experimenters A 选项 Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters 完整对应定位句的两个关键点：irrationally 对应 slavishly/irrationally，every action of the experimenters 对应 every action they'd witnessed。 B) 答非所问 Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one 描述黑猩猩能区分透明与不透明盒子——这是 P8 黑猩猩对比段的隐含信息，但题干问的是作者认为 odd 的发现，奇怪在儿童这边，不在黑猩猩能不能区分上。 C) 无中生有 Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did 提到黑猩猩比儿童更快取得食物——这种速度比较在文中没有任何描写。 D) 与原文相反 Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it 说儿童跳过了敲打这一步——与 children carefully copied all the steps 完全相反，且 P8 显示是黑猩猩在透明条件下才跳过这一步。

records.stem: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?

options.text: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.
It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.
It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.
It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 题干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying? 明确指向某专家对某行为的解释，属于署名+原因型细节题。
【拆句】 主干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying，anthropologist 是 Joseph Henrich 的同位语；preference for copying 名词化结构相当于 prefer to copy。
【定位】 P10 Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers. 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。
【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It originates in the rationality of people around the world 说模仿源于人们的理性——可文中明确说 no one can learn them rationally，恰恰是 没法理性学 才需要模仿；选项把因果反过来了。 B) ✓ 正确 people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers ↔ It stems from the way people learn complex technologies technologies that are often so complex ↔ complex technologies rely on technologies ↔ stems from B It stems from the way people learn complex technologies 把 Henrich 的两步因果（技术复杂 → 必须一步步模仿）压缩成 模仿源于学习复杂技术的方式，与预判完全吻合。 C) 过度推断 It results from people distrusting their own wisdom——文章里只有 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers，即信任 前辈与同伴 的智慧，并未说 不信任自己的智慧；distrust their own 是过度推断 + 与原文相反的合成。 D) 偷换概念 It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step 把 step by step 抄过来，但说成 是因为人有一步步获取知识的欲望——文章是说 因为技术太复杂、不得不 一步步学习，并不是出于 欲望。手段被替换成动机。

records.stem: What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?

options.text: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.
It is characteristic of human beings to copy others.
It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers.
It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （推断题）
【判型】 What point does the author want to emphasize 询问的是作者借这句反语想强调什么，属典型推断题。
【拆句】 题干主干 What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?，when 引导时间状语从句，指明这句话所在的语境；需要把 not chimpanzees 当作对照、推出人类的特征。
【选项】 A) 偷换概念 It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation 把作者的话理解为 模仿是否该避免是个值得讨论的问题——但作者并没有在讨论 是否该避免，而是直接调侃那些反模仿者；arguable（有争议的）是无中生有的态度。 B) ✓ 正确 We're not chimpanzees, after all ↔ It is characteristic of human beings to copy others carefully copying others ↔ to copy others B It is characteristic of human beings to copy others 恰好把反语还原为正面陈述：模仿是人类的特征；其余三项要么没抓到反语指向、要么停留在字面。 C) 以偏概全 It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers 来自 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers——这只是 Henrich 一段的局部解释，不是末段反语 We're not chimpanzees 想强调的点；末段强调的是 人类天性模仿，不是 信任前辈这件事好不好。 D) 与原文相反 It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity 说嘲笑追求不从众的人是天真的——可文中作者恰恰说 you might laugh a little bit，即可以笑一笑，作者站的是支持嘲笑那一方；naive（天真的）正话反说。

records.stem: In the long term, the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited, especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population.
records.explanation:

records.stem: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?

options.text: Its critics' voice has not been heard throughout the country.
There seem to be no other options available to replace it.
The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective? 用 Why 直接问原因，是要回到原文找一句明确解释。
【拆句】 主句 Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular 加状语从句 though ineffective——though 后省略了 it is，完整是 though it is ineffective；六级常用 though 引出让步状语，识别它是看懂题干逻辑的关键。
【定位】 P2 And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals. 尽管对减税的崇拜招致了许多批评，但它（在政策市场上）没有明显的替代品。
【选项】 A) 无中生有 原文只说 the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics——招致很多批评，没有说这些批评"未被全国听见"。 B) ✓ 正确 it lacks for obvious rivals ↔ There seem to be no other options available to replace it. B 项是 it lacks for obvious rivals 的同义重写，与预判完全吻合。 C) 以偏概全 原文 One of the great successes of the Republican Party 明确只是共和党在传播，选项扩大为 all policymakers（所有政策制定者）。 D) 无中生有 原文只说该公式 doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity，并未说大众"误解"了这个公式。

records.stem: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.?

options.text: Aiding people left behind by economic growth.
Prioritizing the growth of the nation's GDP.
Introducing even more extensive tax cuts.

records.explanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）
【判型】 What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.? 直接问作者认为有效的措施，原文必有一句明确给出。
【拆句】 主句 What does the author think，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.；六级常考插入语式的 author think，识别它后面才是真正提问的内容。
【定位】 P5 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 提高美国工人的工资，应当是经济政策制定者的首要任务。
【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. 这是作者描述民主党的做法，紧接着 P4 就把它否定为"政治问题"。 B) 与原文相反 We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP)——作者明确说应少关注 GDP 增长。 C) ✓ 正确 Raising the wages of American workers ↔ Increasing the compensation for labor. C 项是 Raising the wages of American workers 的逐字同义改写，与预判完全吻合。 D) 与原文相反 全文要驳斥的就是减税公式（tax cuts），作者不可能反过来主张更大规模减税。

evidence.text: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers

records.stem: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?

options.text: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.
Paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce attracts more customers.
Consumption stimulates the desire for higher wages.
Familiar arguments for higher wages are outdated.

records.explanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）
【判型】 What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint? 用 What 直接问支撑作者观点的逻辑机制，原文应有明确陈述。
【拆句】 What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?——underlying 是现在分词作后置定语，修饰 logic，等于 that underlies；六级阅读高频，看到 -ing 后置定语要意识到它修饰前面那个名词。
【定位】 P8 Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. 消费驱动着美国经济，而薪酬越高的工人能消费得越多。
【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 workers who are paid more can spend more ↔ The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy. Consumption drives the American economy ↔ ultimately boosts the nation's economy A 项用 ultimately 把 P8 的两句话压成一句因果，与预判的"加薪→消费→经济增长"完全一致。 B) 偷换概念 He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. 是福特出于产能目的支付溢价；The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. 中"工人变顾客"是意外结果，并非"支付溢价"直接导向"吸引更多顾客"。 C) 与原文相反 原文 workers who are paid more can spend more 是高工资 → 高消费，选项反成"消费刺激加薪欲望"，因果链方向倒置。 D) 过度推断 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness.——作者只是说"暂且搁置"公平这一旧论据，并未说它过时。

evidence.text: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more

distractor_explanations.B: 偷换概念：He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. 是福特出于产能目的支付溢价；The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. 中"工人变顾客"是意外结果，并非"支付溢价"直接导向"吸引更多顾客"。

records.stem: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?

options.text: The unerring judgment of market forces.

records.explanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）
【判型】 What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom? 用 What 直问按传统观点加薪的依据，回原文找明确陈述句。
【拆句】 主句 What is the basis for higher wages + 介词短语 according to the conventional wisdom——according to 引出陈述主体，意味着答案要看 conventional wisdom 那方怎么说，而非作者本人怎么说；六级常借这个介词短语区分立场，须警觉。
【定位】 P10 The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。
【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. 中"公平"是作者列出的另一种加薪理由（且被搁置），与 conventional wisdom 无关。 B) ✓ 正确 productivity growth ↔ Increase in productivity. B 项就是 productivity growth 的同义改写，与预判直接对应。 C) 张冠李戴 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 是作者本人的主张，不是传统观点对加薪基础的判断。 D) 张冠李戴 Mainstream economists insist that ... compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. 是主流经济学家的判断，且原文中"市场力量的无误判断"是指工资水平的决定方式，不是加薪的依据。

evidence.text: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages
